A multi-stage build uses a large toolbox to build the app, then copies only the finished app into a smaller runtime image.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Prepare your computer

Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers enabled and the .NET10 SDK. For the full SQL Server stack use supported x64 hardware with enough memory for SQL Server. WPF does not run in the Linux ASP.NET image. Accept applicable vendor licences yourself during installation. Run docker version and docker compose version in a terminal; start Docker Desktop if the engine cannot be reached.

Read Api/Dockerfile line by line

  • FROM sdk:10.0 AS build includes the compiler and restore tools. WORKDIR chooses the working folder.
  • COPY StudyLab.csproj then RUN dotnet restore caches dependency download until project references change. COPY . . brings in source.
  • dotnet publish -c Release -o /out --no-restore creates deployment output.
  • FROM aspnet:10.0 starts the smaller runtime stage. COPY --from=build copies published output, not the whole SDK.
  • ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080 chooses the container HTTP port. EXPOSE documents it; it does not publish a host port.
  • USER $APP_UID uses the non-root app account provided by the Microsoft image. ENTRYPOINT starts StudyLab.dll.

Build from the correct folder

cd Api
dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate
docker build -t studylab-api:1 .

Generate the migration once using the matching dotnet-ef tool before building; the source project includes the SQL Server Design/provider packages. The dot at the end is the build context. .dockerignore excludes bin,obj,.env and local databases. Expected: build steps finish and studylab-api:1 appears in docker image ls.

Try it yourself

Why copy the csproj before all source files?

Worked answer

A source-only change can reuse the dependency-restore layer instead of restoring every time.

Why does COPY fail when building from the repository root?

Worked answer

The Dockerfile paths are relative to its build context. Run from Api or pass the intended context and Dockerfile paths.
